results.summary:
The drawer now draws the focused card's dependency subgraph as inline SVG, above "Blocked by". PR #110 (draft), branch worktree-kb-108-1.

It is a rendering change only: `cardOf` already puts `blockedBy: [{number, title, done}]` on every /api/board card, so there is no new route, no new fetch, no server change, no dependency and no new file. src/serve.js and src/tasks.js are untouched.

What the picture is: the focused card, its transitive blockers, everything transitively waiting on it, and every edge the board knows *between* those nodes — that last part is what makes a diamond come out as a diamond and makes the picture identical opened from either end. A finished blocker is not a board card (fetchBoard reads open issues only), so it becomes a node from the stub the cards that name it carry. Nodes fill from the column colours via `--col` (no second palette) and are `data-open` anchors reusing the blocker list's handler (no second open path). Nothing renders when a card has neither blockers nor a waiting parent.

Two pure top-level functions in the page's single classic <script>: `depGraph(cards, focus)` returns {nodes, edges, rows, width, height, truncated, incomplete} with layers and coordinates on the nodes; `graphSvg(g)` renders it. Longest-path layering + two barycenter passes, cycle-guarded, capped at 40 nodes with a note. Keeping them classic and top-level is deliberate: a module <script> would make `new vm.Script(PAGE_SCRIPT)` throw and take every page test with it.

The incomplete-history case is handled without touching tasks.js: `edgesMayBeMissing` reads the REST-fallback fingerprint off the payload (edges exist, and none hang off a card that is neither todo nor blocked) and the graph carries a one-line note instead of drawing a confidently wrong history.

For the next worker: the vm harness returns objects from the *vm realm*, so `assert.deepEqual` on `g.nodes.map(...)` fails on prototype identity — spread into this realm first ([...g.nodes].map(...)). Browser automation was denied in this session, so the visual check was done numerically (a script printed rows, coordinates and an ASCII picture; the 12-node case lays out 266x192px, well inside the 528px drawer, with no overlapping nodes in a row). The graph has not been seen in a real browser — worth one look at `hkb serve` before the PR leaves draft.
